questions.question: What is MCP (Model Context Protocol)?
choices: A new programming language for AI models
A standardized protocol that enables AI models to discover, connect to, and use external tools and data sources through a common interface
A database management system for storing embeddings
A method for compressing model weights
questions.explanation: MCP provides a universal standard for AI-tool communication. Instead of building custom integrations for each tool, MCP defines a common protocol so any compatible AI model can connect to any compatible tool — like USB for AI.

questions.question: What does an MCP tool definition typically include?
choices: Only the tool's name and a description
A name, description, input schema (parameters), and the function to execute when the tool is called
The complete source code of the tool
questions.explanation: An MCP tool definition provides: a name for identification, a natural language description so the AI understands when to use it, a JSON schema defining input parameters, and the execution handler that performs the actual work.

questions.question: Why is MCP important for the AI ecosystem?
choices: It makes AI models run faster
It creates a standard that prevents vendor lock-in and allows any AI model to use any tool, fostering interoperability and reducing duplicated integration work
It replaces the need for APIs entirely
It only works with one specific AI provider
questions.explanation: MCP standardizes tool integration, so tool developers build once and it works with any MCP-compatible AI, while AI developers support MCP once and gain access to all compatible tools. This eliminates the N×M integration problem.
